AND SHALL THE EXPENDITURES BE MONITORED BY AN INDEPENDENT BOARD-APPOINTED CITIZENS’ OVERSIGHT COMMITTEE TO REVIEW AND CONFIRM THAT ALL FUNDS ARE USED ONLY FOR VOTER APPROVED PROJECTS, WITH NO MONEY GOING TO ADMINISTRATOR SALARIES; SUCH DEBT TO BE EVIDENCED BY THE ISSUANCE OF GENERAL OBLIGATION BONDS TO BE SOLD IN ONE SERIES OR MORE, FOR A PRICE ABOVE OR BELOW THE PRINCIPAL AMOUNT OF SUCH SERIES, ON TERMS AND CONDITIONS AND WITH SUCH MATURITIES AS PERMITTED BY LAW, INCLUDING PROVISIONS FOR REDEMPTION OF THE BONDS PRIOR TO MATURITY WITH OR WITHOUT PAYMENT OF THE PREMIUM; measures.questionText: SHALL COLORADO SPRINGS SCHOOL DISTRICT 11 DEBT BE INCREASED $775 MILLION, WITH A REPAYMENT COST OF NOT TO EXCEED $1.48 BILLION, AND SHALL DISTRICT TAXES BE INCREASED NOT MORE THAN $49.8 MILLION ANNUALLY TO PAY SUCH DEBT, ALL FOR THE PURPOSE OF PROVIDING CAPITAL IMPROVEMENTS FOR DISTRICT PURPOSES, INCLUDING BUT NOT LIMITED TO: • ATTRACTING AND RETAINING HIGH-QUALITY TEACHERS BY INCREASING SALARIES WITH MONEY SAVED BY ACQUIRING ENCUMBERED FACILITIES THROUGH EXERCISING THE DISTRICT'S OPTION TO PREPAY ANY LEASE PURCHASE FINANCINGS; • RENOVATING CAREER AND TECHNICAL EDUCATION FACILITIES THAT PREPARE STUDENTS FOR JOBS IN HEALTHCARE, ENGINEERING, SKILLED TRADES, AND TECHNOLOGY; • REMOVING HAZARDOUS MATERIALS, INCLUDING ASBESTOS AND LEAD PIPES; • INSTALLING MODERN COOLING, HEATING, AND AIR-FILTRATION SYSTEMS IN DISTRICT SCHOOLS; • IMPROVING SCHOOL AND STUDENT SAFETY AND SECURITY; • RENOVATING ALL DISTRICT SCHOOLS INCLUDING SIGNIFICANT RENOVATIONS TO DOHERTY, CORONADO, MITCHELL, AND PALMER HIGH SCHOOLS; AND SHALL THE EXPENDITURES BE MONITORED BY AN INDEPENDENT BOARD-APPOINTED CITIZENS’ OVERSIGHT COMMITTEE TO REVIEW AND CONFIRM THAT ALL FUNDS ARE USED ONLY FOR VOTER APPROVED PROJECTS, WITH NO MONEY GOING TO ADMINISTRATOR SALARIES; AND FOR ACQUIRING, CONSTRUCTING OR IMPROVING ANY CAPITAL ASSETS AUTHORIZED BY LAW; AND SHALL THE MILL LEVY BE IMPOSED IN ANY YEAR WITHOUT LIMITATION AS TO RATE BUT ONLY IN AN AMOUNT SUFFICIENT TO PAY THE PRINCIPAL, PREMIUM, AND INTEREST ON SUCH DEBT OR ANY REFUNDING DEBT (OR TO CREATE A RESERVE FOR SUCH PAYMENT); SUCH DEBT TO BE EVIDENCED BY THE ISSUANCE OF GENERAL OBLIGATION BONDS TO BE SOLD IN ONE SERIES OR MORE, FOR A PRICE ABOVE OR BELOW THE PRINCIPAL AMOUNT OF SUCH SERIES, ON TERMS AND CONDITIONS AND WITH SUCH MATURITIES AS PERMITTED BY LAW, INCLUDING PROVISIONS FOR REDEMPTION OF THE BONDS PRIOR TO MATURITY WITH OR WITHOUT PAYMENT OF THE PREMIUM; AND SHALL THE REVENUES FROM SUCH DEBT AND TAXES AND ANY EARNINGS FROM THE INVESTMENT THEREOF BE COLLECTED AND SPENT AS A VOTER APPROVED REVENUE CHANGE UNDER ARTICLE X, SECTION 20 OF THE COLORADO CONSTITUTION AND ANY OTHER LAW?

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Raise Denver Public Schools property taxes by up to $44 million in tax year 2026, collected in 2027, and annually afterward for education. Uses include educator pay, career and technical courses in high-demand fields, student mental health and special education. The added property-tax levy, combined with earlier voter-approved override levies, would reach the district’s limit under state law. Money would go into the general fund in addition to existing property taxes. Spending would appear in the district’s annual independent audit on its website. Investment earnings would be exempt from Colorado’s constitutional revenue limits.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve the additional property taxes for education, the annual audit reporting and the revenue-limit exception for investment earnings.
measureRecords.noMeans: Do not approve this additional property-tax levy or its proposed revenue-limit exception.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Create a 0.333% sales and use tax in the Front Range Passenger Rail District to build, operate and maintain Colorado Connector passenger rail, station improvements and connections to stations. The service would connect Front Range communities from Pueblo to Fort Collins. State-law exemptions would apply, including gasoline, food, residential electricity and gas, prescription drugs and medical supplies. The measure authorizes $295 million in annual taxes, with amounts raised in later years allowed to vary, and $580 million in debt with a repayment cost of $785 million. Tax revenue, contributions and investment income could be kept outside Colorado’s constitutional revenue limits. An independent auditor and a rotating group of district taxpayers would review dedicated revenue each year.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve the sales and use tax, borrowing, revenue-limit exception and annual reviews for the district’s passenger rail program.
measureRecords.noMeans: Do not authorize this sales and use tax, borrowing or revenue-limit exception.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Increase Manitou Springs’ excise tax on ticket sales and admission fees from 5% to 9.03%, starting January 1, 2027. The added 4.03 percentage points would raise an estimated $1,128,000 in the first full fiscal year and whatever amounts the tax raises in later years. The city could keep and spend the added revenue despite Colorado’s constitutional revenue and spending limits or other legal limits.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve the higher ticket and admission tax and permission to keep and spend its revenue outside those limits.
measureRecords.noMeans: Do not approve the 4.03-percentage-point increase; keep the existing 5% tax rate.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Raise Monument’s use tax on construction and building materials and construction equipment from 2% to 3.5%, beginning January 1, 2027. The tax applies when a building or right-of-way permit is requested and a 3.5% municipal sales tax was not collected where the items were bought. Existing exemptions in Ordinance 19-2026 and the municipal code would still apply. The increase would raise $2,272,500 annually initially, with later revenue varying with collections. All revenue would fund capital projects, including streets, roads, bridges, sidewalks and stormwater improvements. The town could retain and spend the revenue and investment earnings outside Colorado’s constitutional revenue limits and other legal limits.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve the use-tax increase for capital projects and the exception to revenue limits.
measureRecords.noMeans: Do not approve this increase; keep the existing 2% use-tax rate.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Add a 0.5% sales tax in Green Mountain Falls from January 1, 2027 through December 31, 2030. It would raise $58,684 in the first full fiscal year, with later amounts based on collections. Revenue would pay for construction, operation and maintenance of the old town marshal’s building at 10545 Ute Pass Avenue. Revenue above those costs could fund other capital improvements. The town could retain and spend tax revenue, interest and investment earnings outside Colorado’s constitutional revenue limits and other legal limits.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve the temporary additional sales tax for the old marshal’s building and, if revenue exceeds its costs, other capital improvements, with the revenue-limit exception.
measureRecords.noMeans: Do not approve this additional sales tax or its proposed revenue-limit exception.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Authorize $775 million in Colorado Springs School District 11 bonds, with total repayment no greater than $1.48 billion, and up to $49.8 million in additional property taxes each year to repay them. The property-tax rate would have no fixed cap but could raise only enough for debt payments or a repayment reserve. Projects include school renovations, career and technical facilities, removal of asbestos and lead pipes, heating and air improvements, safety and security, and other school capital assets. Paying off lease-purchase financing for facilities could free existing money for teacher pay. An independent, board-appointed citizens’ committee would review spending; no bond money could go to administrator salaries. Debt and tax revenue and investment earnings could be spent outside Colorado’s constitutional revenue limits.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve the bonds, taxes to repay them, project restrictions, citizen oversight and revenue-limit exception.
measureRecords.noMeans: Do not authorize these bonds, the additional taxes to repay them or the related revenue-limit exception.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Authorize $80 million in Cheyenne Mountain School District 12 bonds, with total repayment capped at $162 million, and up to $8.8 million in additional property taxes annually for capital improvements. Projects include school safety, more learning space at Broadmoor and Cheyenne Mountain elementary schools, replacing Skyway Elementary on its existing site, athletic and activity fields, and building systems. Other lawful school capital assets could also be funded. The property-tax rate would have no fixed cap but could raise only enough for debt payments or a repayment reserve. Bonds could be repaid early with a premium of no more than 3%. Debt and tax revenue and investment earnings could be kept and spent outside Colorado’s constitutional revenue limits.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve the school bonds, property taxes to repay them and the related revenue-limit exception.
measureRecords.noMeans: Do not authorize these bonds, the additional property taxes or the related revenue-limit exception.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Add a 4-mill property-tax levy in Hanover School District 28 for education, including staff pay, hiring and retaining teachers and support staff, and employee benefits. It would raise $231,788 in tax year 2026 for collection in 2027, with later revenue based on taxable property values. The levy would be added to taxes already authorized for the general fund. The district could keep and spend its revenue and investment earnings outside Colorado’s constitutional revenue limits.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve the additional property-tax levy for education and its revenue-limit exception.
measureRecords.noMeans: Do not approve this additional property-tax levy or its proposed revenue-limit exception.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Increase Peyton Fire Protection District’s property-tax rate by 4.85 mills beginning January 1, 2027, to raise $327,903 annually or the amount the levy produces. Money would support fire, ambulance, emergency medical, rescue and safety services, including full-time firefighters, emergency medical technicians and paramedics, vehicles and equipment, and updated facilities. Revenue and investment earnings would have a permanent exception from Colorado’s constitutional revenue limits and statutory property-tax limits.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve the additional property-tax levy for district emergency services and the permanent revenue-limit exceptions.
measureRecords.noMeans: Do not approve this property-tax increase or its proposed permanent revenue-limit exceptions.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Increase Elbert Fire Protection District taxes by $497,646 in collection year 2027 and annually afterward until collection year 2051. Revenue would be dedicated to designing, acquiring, building, completing, equipping and financing new fire stations. Separately, waive the 5.25% property-tax limit on all district taxes in all future years, including after the station tax ends.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve the taxes for new fire stations through collection year 2051 and permanently waive the 5.25% property-tax limit for all district taxes.
measureRecords.noMeans: Do not approve this fire-station tax increase or the permanent waiver of the 5.25% property-tax limit.
